title: Why violet flowers set more seed
bodyMd: Plant ecologist Tomasz Wieland studies a meadow herb whose flowers are either white or violet. In the meadow, violet-flowered plants set about 40 percent more seed than white-flowered plants, and bumblebees visit violet flowers far more often. Wieland suspects that bee preference is not the whole explanation: the violet pigment, which also colors the plant's seed capsules, absorbs ultraviolet light and may shield the developing seeds from damage. To test this idea, he grew plants of both colors in full sun under fine netting that kept all insects out but let sunlight through, and he pollinated every flower by hand with the same amount of pollen.
